brief: A workbench organizer: two storeys, bins on top, a drawer below, all edges capped.

requirements.evidence: 2 stacks of bases with divided bins and a drawer, dressed with a few small tools (pens, markers, brush, electrical tape).
Level 0 and level 1 at both (0,0) and (1,0): piece:0,0,0/0,0,1 (north halves) and piece:1,0,0/1,0,1 (full bases).
bin:0,0,1 (3 compartments) and bin:1,0,1 (2 compartments) on the upper storey.
drawer:0#0,0#cut on the cut face of the level-0 half base, shown open with tape inside.
Capping every open face added 13 solid end caps, and the final check reported no open faces. The joints are bolted too.

finish.summary:
I built a two-storey workbench organizer. It's two stacks of bases side by side, with bins on the upper storey and a drawer in the lower storey, and every open edge is capped. The final check passed with no rule issues, and the collision check came back clear.

- **Left stack:** two north-half bases stacked. The drawer sits on the cut face of the bottom one. I used half bases there because only they offered a drawer spot, and a half base only takes another half base on top, so the upper one is a half too. It holds a full-depth bin split into 3 compartments.
- **Right stack:** two full bases stacked. The upper one holds a full-depth bin split into 2 compartments. The bottom one has no drawer, since a full base offered no drawer spot.
- **Finishing:** I capped all the open faces with solid end caps (13 caps) and bolted the joints together. The build comes to 35 parts, about 2,068 g of filament and roughly 2,960 minutes of printing.
- **Props:** pens, markers and a paint brush stand in the bins, and a roll of electrical tape is in the drawer, which I left open so you can see it. The longer tools (screwdriver, hand file, hex driver) wouldn't stay upright in the compartments, so I left them out.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
